title: Mobile App Development in South Carolina
metaTitle: Mobile App Development in South Carolina | TDM
metaDescription: iOS and Android app development for South Carolina businesses: native Swift and Kotlin or cross-platform Flutter and React Native, from UX research to store release.
lead: TDM (The Digital Marketing Services) designs and builds iOS and Android apps for South Carolina businesses and startups. We build native apps in Swift and Kotlin, and cross-platform apps in Flutter or React Native, and we take each one from UX research through to release on the App Store and Google Play. In this state an app usually has a practical job: serving visitors on the coast, workers on a plant floor, drivers on the road, or students and patients who would rather not phone.

sections.heading: Who uses apps in South Carolina, and for what
paragraphs: Along the coast, the user is often a visitor. Someone staying a week in Myrtle Beach, on Hilton Head or in downtown Charleston wants to book a tee time, a charter, a table or a tour from a phone, and will not create an account to do it. Apps for that audience have to be quick on a first visit and useful without a tutorial.

In the Upstate and around the port, the user is more often an employee. Manufacturers and logistics firms use mobile apps for inspections, deliveries, stock counts and maintenance requests, on devices that get dropped and in buildings with patchy signal. That means large touch targets, offline support and syncing that does not lose a record.

Columbia, Clemson and Charleston add students, patients and public-sector users. University towns produce startups with a first product to test, and health providers want appointment and messaging tools that people will actually open.

sections.heading: Native or cross-platform
paragraphs: This is the first decision, and it is about money and performance, not fashion. Native development in Swift for iOS and Kotlin with Jetpack Compose for Android gives the best performance and platform feel. It suits apps with live maps, heavy device use or demanding interfaces. Cross-platform development in Flutter or React Native puts one codebase on both stores, which suits a first version, a booking app or a content and commerce app where speed to market and budget lead.

sections.heading: What the work includes
paragraphs: What separates an app that gets used from one that gets deleted is decided before any code is written. Every project begins with research into the people who will use it.
bullets: UX research: user personas, journey mapping and wireframes, then a design system and full interface design.
Development in the chosen stack, built in stages you can see and test.
Backend and APIs: authentication, payments, push notifications and live features such as GPS tracking, chat and order status.
Testing on real devices, not only simulators.
Submission and release through the App Store and Google Play.
Support and further releases after launch.

sections.heading: Questions to settle before you hire anyone
paragraphs: Decide whether you need an app at all. For many local businesses a fast mobile website does the job, and we will say so. If you do need one, ask who holds the developer accounts and source code, since both should be yours. Ask how seasonal load is handled if your busy months are spring and summer on the Grand Strand. And if the app touches health information, student records or payments, say so at the start so that privacy and security requirements are designed in.

presence: A member of our team is based in South Carolina. Research, design and engineering are carried out remotely by our wider team, with regular demos so you can see the app take shape and test builds on your own phone.

faqs.q: Do you build both iPhone and Android apps?
faqs.a: Yes. We build native iOS apps in Swift, native Android apps in Kotlin with Jetpack Compose, and cross-platform apps in Flutter or React Native that run on both from one codebase. The choice depends on your users, features and budget.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to build an app in South Carolina?
faqs.a: It depends on the features, the number of platforms and the backend the app needs. We quote after a free consultation, once the scope is clear.

faqs.q: How long does app development take?
faqs.a: It depends on your requirements and the brief. A simple booking app and a marketplace with live tracking are very different projects. The timeline is agreed in the project plan before development starts.

faqs.q: Can you build an app that works without a signal?
faqs.a: Yes. Offline support is a design decision made early: the app stores data on the device and syncs when a connection returns. It is common for warehouse, plant and field apps, and for use in rural parts of the state.
